64c6e0.conditions: 49-byte subscripts exceed the 32-byte inline limit, so they travel as separate ADLB_TAG_SYNC_SUB messages; with eager buffering of these small sends, every interleaving is handled
64c6e0.reasoning: Subscripts longer than SYNC_DATA_SIZE are sent after the sync header with a blocking SEND tagged ADLB_TAG_SYNC_SUB and received with RECV(rank, ADLB_TAG_SYNC_SUB). The sync headers are matched through the ANY_SOURCE ring of irecvs in the order they were posted, and they are processed in that order. A header that rank 2 defers while it is in its own sync loop goes into the FIFO pending list, which is drained after every handler, after a steal, and during the idle check (SUBSCRIBE counts as a pending notification). So subscripts from the same sender are taken in send order. All remote subscribes target container 2, so even a permutation would not change anything. xlb_poll skips SYNC_SUB messages, so a stray subscript is never dispatched as a request. The SEND-SEND cycle between the servers that the code warns about needs unbuffered 49-byte sends, which Open MPI's eager protocol rules out, and it needs implausible late subscribes. Barriers and the client-side notifications order the stores.
